analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds one paragraph (head lines 253-260). The paragraph says the SSD stage runs before engine.submit, off the engine queue, and that a provider-staged complete-checkpoint import creates its destinations already available from host bytes without evaluating or fencing them, so it does not wait on the engine's evalLock. It points to CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift (CBv2CompleteCheckpointImport) and the ssd-kv-cache.md#complete-checkpoint-payload anchor. No code, config, key handling, TTL, HMAC naming, salt scoping, disk budget or kill-switch semantics change here. The described behavior is an availability/latency optimization on the SSD prefix-cache staging path (T-041, TB-007, A-001). The patch shows no change to the at-rest crypto, K_lookup derivation, cacheSalt scoping or SEC-035 accepted-risk posture. Unverified: the actual source change in CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift is not in this batch. The next pass should check that destinations built from host bytes still pass DBK3 AES-GCM authentication, model/layout bindings and the cacheSalt scope before they become adoptable. It should also check that skipping eval/fence does not create unfenced reads of buffers that are still being mutated, or leak a staged prefix across scopes. This documentation-only change gives no evidence of regression, so no findings are reported. Residual uncertainty comes only from the missing code.
